title: Single-cell sequencing protocol for studying NF1 nerve sheath tumors
author: Zhang, Gopalan, et al.
materials: EasySep Human CD56 Positive Selection Kit II

steps.title: Prepare DNase I solution
steps.instruction: Make 1× DNase I buffer by diluting 10× DNase I buffer with HBSS, reconstitute lyophilized DNase I with 20 mL of this buffer to obtain 100 Kunitz U/mL, aliquot 200 µL, and store at –80 °C (stable 1 year).

steps.title: Prepare sterile tumor dissociation media
steps.instruction: Weigh dispase II and collagenase I, dissolve them in DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS and penicillin‑streptomycin‑glutamine, filter the enzyme cocktail through a 0.22 µm filter, and keep at 4 °C.

steps.title: Warm dissociation media to 37°C
steps.instruction: Place the sterile tumor dissociation media in a water bath or incubator until it reaches 37 °C.

steps.title: Add DNase I to media
steps.instruction: Add DNase I solution to the warmed dissociation media at a ratio of 100 µL DNase I per 10 mL media.

steps.title: Gather tissue processing tools
steps.instruction: In the laminar flow hood, set out a 10 mL syringe, a gentleMACS™ c‑tube, a scalpel, sterile tweezers, a 60 mm tissue‑culture dish, and a 40 µm cell strainer. Ensure at least 10 mL of complete dissociation media per specimen (scale up as needed).

steps.title: Demultiplex and align reads with CellRanger
steps.instruction: Run cellranger mkfastq (v6.0.0) to convert Illumina BCL files to FASTQ, then run cellranger count using reference refdata‑gex‑GRCh38‑2020‑A to align reads, filter, and generate barcode/UMI count matrices.

steps.title: Correct ambient RNA using SoupX
steps.instruction: Load each lane’s count matrix into SoupX, manually test contamination fractions of 10 %, 20 %, 30 % and 40 %, generate corrected matrices, inspect known cell‑type markers (e.g., CD79B for B cells) to select the appropriate fraction, and save the chosen corrected matrix for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Predict and remove doublets with Scrublet
steps.instruction: For each capture lane, compute the expected doublet rate as (cells captured / 10 000) × 0.8 %; run Scrublet’s scr.Scrublet function with this rate, then discard cells flagged as doublets.

steps.title: Integrate and cluster data with Seurat
steps.instruction: In Seurat (v15) filter out low‑quality cells (nFeature_RNA > 6000 or mitochondrial % > 20 %). Normalize with LogNormalize (scale.factor = 10 000), find the top 3000 variable genes (method = vst), assign cell‑cycle scores, identify integration anchors (dims = 1:40), perform anchor‑based rPCA, scale data regressing out percent.mt, nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, S.Score, G2M.Score, run PCA (npcs = 40), UMAP (dims = 1:40), FindNeighbors (dims = 1:40), FindClusters (resolution = 0.8), and finally call FindAllMarkers (only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25) to obtain cluster biomarkers.

steps.title: Annotate cell types manually
steps.instruction: Examine the cluster‑specific marker genes identified in the previous step and assign cell‑type identities based on known marker expression.

steps.title: Compute signature genes per cell type
steps.instruction: For each cell type, select up to 300 signature genes that are markers from the previous analysis with an adjusted p‑value < 0.1.

steps.title: Identify Schwann and MPNST markers
steps.instruction: Using Seurat’s FindMarkers (only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25), derive marker genes for neoplastic Schwann cells and for malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) cells.

steps.title: Score signature activity with AUCell
steps.instruction: Apply the AUCell function from the SCENIC package to compute activity scores for each signature gene set in every cell.

steps.title: Compare AUCell activities via Wilcoxon test
steps.instruction: Perform a two‑sided Wilcoxon test to compare AUCell activity distributions of developmental Schwann cell types between MPNST malignant cells and Schwann cells from the patient dataset.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for single-cell RNA sequencing of a single-cell suspension obtained from fresh NF1-associated nerve sheath tumors. Transcriptomic profiling of all cell types on a single-cell level is a powerful tool to understand the intra-tumoral heterogeneity of these tumors. This protocol can be used on both fresh surgical specimens as well as patient-derived xenografts to profile the transcriptome on a single-cell level.2
